churn_resistance.rationale: The data layer is properly fenced off in one module with no framework internals or copy-pasted boilerplate, which limits upgrade ripple; but the boundary between that module and the routes is almost entirely 'any' despite typegen being wired up, and the not-found sentinel plus full-dataset home loader are patterns likely to need rework when requirements or data move.

findings.issue: Loaders and components are typed 'any' (pokemon.tsx:17,22,36; move.tsx:11,26; ability.tsx:12; type-detail.tsx:13; 2 in type-detail.tsx) although generated route types exist — tsconfig.json:2,15 configures .react-router/types but no route imports './+types/...' or uses Route.LoaderArgs/Route.ComponentProps
findings.suggestion: Use 'import type { Route } from "./+types/<name>"' with Route.LoaderArgs/Route.ComponentProps per react-router/docs/how-to/route-module-type-safety.md, so loader-data drift is caught at compile time

findings.issue: Not-found is a hand-rolled { notFound: true } sentinel returned from the loader (also move.tsx:9, ability.tsx:9, type-detail.tsx:6) instead of the documented 'throw data("Not Found", { status: 404 })' + route ErrorBoundary, and the app never sends HTTP 404 for missing records
findings.suggestion: Throw data(..., { status: 404 }) from loaders and render the record pages' 404 UI from a route ErrorBoundary (with isRouteErrorResponse), which is both the documented pattern and gets the encouraged 404 status

findings.issue: No ErrorBoundary anywhere in the app: an API failure (api.server.ts:32-33 throws on non-ok responses) renders the framework default error page, whose '💿 Hey developer 👋' message ships to production (app/build/client/assets/jsx-runtime-*.js:14)
findings.suggestion: Add a root ErrorBoundary and per-route boundaries for the record pages so API outages show app-styled errors

findings.issue: Home loader returns the full 1025-species dataset (name, humanized name, sprite URL, type objects, generation per species) which is embedded in the HTML for every request; the framework docs recommend filtering URL-driven state in the loader so the payload stays bounded as data grows
findings.suggestion: Parse q/type/generation/page in the loader (request.url.searchParams) and return only the 48-card page; client-side filtering can stay for the instant debounced search UX via clientLoader or local state

findings.issue: fetchJson never forwards request.signal / uses AbortController, so aborted SSR requests keep upstream fetches running and a shared promise cache can hold results of abandoned requests
findings.suggestion: Thread the loader's request.signal into fetchJson calls for request-scoped fetches; per-key cached fetches can ignore it, but per-request lookups should be cancellable

findings.issue: cardSprite hardcodes 'id <= 1025' to construct sprite URLs from the documented pattern instead of reading sprites.front_default from the API, coupling the app to the current snapshot size (a code comment acknowledges this; a fallback fetch handles new ids)
findings.suggestion: Read the sprite URL from the API's sprites.front_default where the pokemon record is already available, keeping the pattern only as a documented last resort

findings.issue: Module-level async IIFE promises (typeInfosPromise, generationInfosPromise, homeDataPromise, versionGroupsPromise) fire API requests at import time; a down API produces an unawaited promise that only surfaces through a loader error
findings.suggestion: Lazily initialize these indexes on first access (e.g. via a memoized getter) so module import has no side effects and failures are scoped to the loaders that need them

findings.issue: recordCache is Map<string, Promise<any>> — the cache stores untyped values, so PokeAPI schema drift inside the single data module is invisible to TypeScript
findings.suggestion: Define minimal interfaces for the PokeAPI resources actually consumed and type the cache Map<string, Promise<Resource | null>>; costs a few type lines and makes the centralized module a real type boundary

summary: A framework app genuinely on the current stable React Router (8.5.1) with zero deprecated APIs, a textbook-minimal dependency set, and all data access fenced behind one module — it will survive framework upgrades with little churn. The forward-looking weaknesses are at the type boundary: generated route types are configured but ignored in favour of 'any', and the not-found/error flow is hand-rolled instead of the documented data()/ErrorBoundary pattern, which also forfeits the 404 status. Fixing typing and error handling would make this a model framework-mode app.

apis.replacement: generate types are configured (tsconfig.json:2,15) but route modules type args as 'any'; adopt './+types/<route>' imports
throw data("Not Found", { status: 404 }) + route ErrorBoundary (react-router skill framework-mode reference, from installed docs)
